deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of the section of Riemann's Göttingen dissertation (1851, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse') that justifies the Dirichlet-principle argument. In the printed dissertation the corresponding text appears, I believe, as Art. 17; here it is numbered §16 (unsure).

The previous section, ad 15, concerns the uniqueness of the minimiser: if Ω' = Ω + L' is also minimal, then L' = 0, so λ' is constant and hence 0. The notation is as follows.
- T is the (possibly multi-sheeted) surface.
- λ is an admissible variation.
- L(λ) = ∫_T (λ_x² + λ_y²) dT is the Dirichlet integral.
- γ is a given discontinuous function.

Claim to be made rigorous: finiteness of L prevents λ from approximating a discontinuous γ arbitrarily closely. Precisely, suppose λ is required to agree with γ outside a region T' that contains the discontinuity set. Then T' can be chosen so small that L > C for any prescribed constant C.

Case 1: point singularity. γ is discontinuous at a point O such that, on part of a circle of radius ρ about O, ρ γ_x and ρ γ_y tend to finite (nonzero) limits or become infinite as ρ → 0. A model is γ = arg(z − O).
- Then there is an R such that for 0 < ρ < R,
  F(ρ) := ρ² ∫_0^{2π} (γ_x² + γ_y²) dφ
  does not vanish. Let a > 0 be its minimum on that interval.
- Take T' to be the disc ρ < r with r < R. On the annulus r < ρ < R we have λ = γ, since the annulus lies outside T'. This step is implicit; I have supplied it.
- The annulus therefore contributes to L the amount
  ∫_r^R dρ ∫_0^{2π} (λ_x² + λ_y²) ρ dφ = ∫_r^R F(ρ)/ρ dρ ≥ ∫_r^R (a/ρ) dρ = a(log R − log r).
- Choosing r = R e^{−C/a} makes this ≥ C; any smaller r makes it > C.
- Hence if T' is bounded by a circle of radius ρ < R e^{−C/a}, the part of L coming from the rest of T already exceeds C. Thus L > C however λ is chosen inside the disc.

Footnote: the argument was written for an ordinary interior point, one that is neither a branch (winding) point nor a boundary point. It needs essential modification only at a boundary point where the boundary has a cusp (Rückkehrpunkt). Even there, fixing a degree of discontinuity that λ cannot attain rests on the same principles, so Riemann only indicates this case.

Case 2: line of discontinuity. Here the page only begins the set-up.
- s is arclength along the line and p is the normal distance.
- κ is the curvature of the line element ds, counted positive when concave toward positive p.
- p_1 and p_2 are the p-values at the boundary of T' on the positive and negative sides.
- γ_1 and γ_2 are the corresponding values of γ.
- The text breaks off at 'Betrachten wir nun irgend eine stetig…'. The intended continuation is presumably a Cauchy–Schwarz estimate across the strip, ∫(∂λ/∂p)² dp ≥ (γ_1 − γ_2)²/(p_1 − p_2), with a curvature correction (1 + κp). That would blow up as the strip shrinks; this is my inference and does not appear on the page.
errors: The value of r as transcribed, R e^{a/C}, is wrong. It exceeds R and gives no bound. The correct choice is r = R e^{-C/a}, since a(log R - log r) ≥ C requires log(R/r) ≥ C/a. Either Riemann slipped in the draft or the transcription misreads the exponent; the printed dissertation has, I believe, e^{-C/a}.

'Nicht Null wird' only says F(ρ) > 0. The argument needs inf F > 0 on (0,R). Calling this inf a 'smallest value' a is a mild unjustified step, since the infimum may not be attained. The stated hypotheses (limits of ρ∂γ finite nonzero, or infinite) make it plausible.
The step 'λ = γ on the annulus' is used without being stated. It is valid because the annulus r<ρ<R lies outside T'.

results.what: Lower bound on the Dirichlet integral of a function with a point singularity of angular type (|∇γ| ~ 1/ρ): the energy in the annulus r<ρ<R is ≥ a log(R/r), which diverges as r→0. So a finite-energy λ cannot approximate such a γ.
results.modern_name: Logarithmic divergence of Dirichlet energy for 1/ρ-gradient singularities (non-membership in H^1; zero capacity of points is the dual statement)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (dissertation 1851) in the context of the Dirichlet principle; later rigorous treatment by Hilbert (1900) and others

results.what: Uniqueness of the minimiser in the Dirichlet principle (from the context page): L(λ')=0 implies λ' is constant, hence 0.
Set-up for the estimate across a line of discontinuity using normal coordinates (s,p) with curvature κ.
results.modern_name: Energy estimate across a jump discontinuity (trace/jump functions are not in H^1)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of a passage of Riemann's published dissertation on the Dirichlet principle; the content is known and credited to him. The only points of interest are a draft-level numbering difference and the possible slip in the exponent.

checkable.asserts: The annulus lower bound integrates to a(log R - log r).
The choice r = R e^{-C/a} makes the bound exactly C, so any smaller r gives > C.
For the model singularity γ = arg z, ρ²|∇γ|² = 1, so F(ρ) = 2π and a = 2π > 0.
The energy of arg z in the annulus diverges (to oo) as r → 0.

transcription_corrections: 'ρ ∂α/∂x und ρ ∂α/∂y' should read 'ρ ∂γ/∂x und ρ ∂γ/∂y'; the condition concerns the given discontinuous function γ.
'nicht einer {+un+}stetigen Function' is followed in the image by 'γ' (a discontinuous function γ). The insertion 'un' is correct.
The exponent in 'r = R e^{a/C}' should mathematically be e^{-C/a}. Check whether the manuscript has a minus sign or inverted fraction; the transcription's '[?]' is warranted.
'enthält man also zur Begrenzung von T'' is more likely 'wählt man also zur Begrenzung von T''.
'um O mit ρ beschriebenen Kreisringes' may be 'Kreises' in the image. The marginal folio number 69 is visible at right.
